raw_case_text:
The patient was a 10-year-old boy with confirmed CGD as an underlying disease at 11 months of age based on hematological and immunological tests (nitroblue-tetrazolium=0). He had several admissions to the Children Medical Center of Tehran, Iran. The patient had a previous history of recurrent episodes of pneumonia for which he was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and long-term prophylaxis, including itraconazole (5 mg/kg/day), along with co-trimoxazole (5 mg/kg/day) and IFN gamma (1.5 mcg/kg). At the age of nine years, the patient was hospitalized for several clinical signs and symptoms, such as knee pain, night sweets, lethargy, coryza, and progressive weakness. 
A plain X-ray imaging showed a soft tissue density destructive lesion in T4-T5 vertebral bodies with adjacent prevertebral soft tissue mass involving the central spinal column. There was also evidence of an expansile lytic lesion involving the right fifth rib, laminectomy of L4-L5 with pedicular screw, along with post-operative changes (Figure 1). Laboratory findings included ESR of 75 mm/h, CRP of 69, white blood cell count of 6000/mm3, monocyte of 37.4%, hemoglobin of 7.8 g/dl, and thrombocyte of 383000/mm3. The results of histopathology and fungal culture obtained from surgical debridement samples revealed the diagnosis of invasive aspergillosis caused by Aspergillus species (Figure 2).
In addition, a microscopic examination showed abundant hull cells and the conidial head pattern of A. nidulans (Figure 2). The specific primer pair 5'-GGT AAC CAA ATC GGT GCT GCT TTC-3' and 5'-ACCCTC AGT GTA GTG ACC CTT GGC-3' was used to amplify beta-tubulin genes and confirm the isolate as A. nidulans [19]. Then, the nucleotide sequence was deposited in GenBank under the accession number MK749954. At this time, the treatment was continued with amphotericin B deoxycholate (1 mg/kg/day) which was subsequently changed to voriconazole (9 mg/kg/day). Finally, caspofungin (50 microg/m2) was also added to the therapy, and the patient was discharged from the hospital. However, after a few months, this case was readmitted because of severe headache, blurred vision, and brain abscess, while receiving voriconazole therapy (200 mg/day). 
Treatment was continued with amphotericin B, caspofungin, voriconazole, and interferon-gamma. Due to the lack of antifungal response and deterioration of the symptoms, he underwent the insertion of a right parietal ventriculoperitoneal shunt. An urgent computed tomography scan of the brain did not depict any damage. However, it revealed the dilation of the left ventricle and dilation of the occipital horn of the right ventricle, along with extensive vasogenic edema in the right temporoparietal lobe (Figure 1). 
In spite of performing aggressive surgery and different treatments, the child passed away within one year. Postmortem antifungal susceptibility profile of the isolate was examined against itraconazole (Sigma-Aldrich Quimica, Madrid, Spain), amphotericin B (Sigma-Aldrich Quimica, Madrid, Spain), and voriconazole (Pfizer SA, Madrid, Spain) using EUCAST method [20]. The in vitro minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of the mentioned antifungals were obtained as 1, > 16, and 0.25 mg/L, respectively. Furthermore, the minimum effective concentration for caspofungin (Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ) was estimated at 1 mg/L. This species was found to show resistance to amphotericin B (MIC>2 mg/L).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 9-year-old boy with chronic granulomatous disease presented with knee pain, night sweats, lethargy, coryza, and progressive weakness, followed several months later by severe headache and blurred vision.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with chronic granulomatous disease at 11 months of age (NBT = 0) and maintained on long-term itraconazole, co-trimoxazole, and interferon-gamma prophylaxis for recurrent pneumonias, the patient was hospitalized at age 9 with knee pain, night sweats, lethargy, coryza, and progressive weakness due to destructive T4-T5 vertebral and right 5th rib osteomyelitis caused by Aspergillus nidulans. Despite surgical debridement and combination voriconazole plus caspofungin, he was readmitted a few months later (at age 10) with severe headache and blurred vision due to a cerebral abscess and hydrocephalus.
subjective.past_medical_history: Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) confirmed at 11 months of age by nitroblue tetrazolium test (NBT = 0); history of recurrent pneumonias and prior L4-L5 laminectomy with pedicle screw fixation; long-term prophylaxis with itraconazole (5 mg/kg/day), co-trimoxazole (5 mg/kg/day), and subcutaneous interferon-gamma (1.5 ug/kg).
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial admission (age 9): knee pain, night sweats, lethargy, coryza, and progressive weakness. Readmission (age 10): severe headache and blurred vision.

objective.physical_examination: Presented at age 9 with lethargy and progressive weakness, and at age 10 with neurological deterioration and visual blurring requiring ventriculoperitoneal shunting.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs at age 9 showed ESR 75 mm/h, CRP 69 mg/L, WBC 6,000/mm3 with monocytosis (37.4% monocytes), anemia (hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL), and platelets 383,000/mm3. Spine and chest radiographs showed a destructive lesion of the T4-T5 vertebral bodies with a prevertebral soft-tissue mass, an expansile lytic lesion of the right 5th rib, and prior L4-L5 laminectomy/pedicle screw hardware.
objective.advanced_workup: Histopathology and fungal culture of surgical spinal/costal debridement specimens demonstrated invasive aspergillosis with abundant Hulle cells and conidial heads characteristic of Aspergillus nidulans, confirmed by beta-tubulin gene PCR sequencing (GenBank accession MK749954). EUCAST antifungal susceptibility testing showed intrinsic resistance to amphotericin B (MIC >16 mg/L), itraconazole MIC 1 mg/L, voriconazole MIC 0.25 mg/L, and caspofungin MEC 1 mg/L. On readmission for severe headache and blurred vision, cranial imaging demonstrated a brain abscess with extensive right temporoparietal vasogenic edema and dilation of the left lateral ventricle and right occipital horn.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Fatal disseminated invasive aspergillosis caused by amphotericin B-resistant Aspergillus nidulans presenting with T4-T5 vertebral osteomyelitis, right 5th rib osteomyelitis, and subsequent right temporoparietal brain abscess and hydrocephalus in a child with chronic granulomatous disease (breaking through itraconazole and IFN-gamma prophylaxis), confirmed by surgical biopsy histopathology, culture showing Hulle cells, beta-tubulin sequencing (MK749954), and EUCAST susceptibility testing. Despite spinal surgical debridement, right parietal ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement, and combination therapy with voriconazole (9 mg/kg/day IV, then 200 mg/day orally), caspofungin (50 ug/m2), amphotericin B deoxycholate, and interferon-gamma, the child died within 1 year.
